stem.text: What is likely to be found in a free trade area?

options.text: import tariffs on goods entering a member country from a country outside the free trade area
import tariffs on goods entering a member country from another member country
quotas on the number of goods entering a member country from another member country
subsidies on goods leaving a member country for another member country

explanation.text: A free trade area removes tariffs and quotas on trade between its own member countries, but — unlike a customs union — each member keeps its own, independent trade policy (including tariffs) toward countries outside the area. So tariffs on goods from non-member countries entering a member country are expected and allowed, while tariffs/quotas between members are not.

optionAnalysis.text: A free trade area does not require members to adopt a common external tariff, so each member can still impose its own tariffs on goods from outside the area.
The whole point of a free trade area is removing tariffs on trade between member countries, so this should not exist within the area.
Similarly, quotas between member countries are removed in a free trade area, not retained.
Export subsidies between members are not a defining feature of a free trade area; free trade areas are about removing trade barriers, not adding subsidies.

reasoningChain: Recall the defining feature of a free trade area: tariffs and quotas are removed on trade between the member countries.
Recall the key distinction from a customs union: a free trade area does not require a common external tariff, so each member can set its own tariffs on non-members.
Identify option A as describing exactly this allowed independent policy toward non-members, while B and C describe barriers that should be absent between members.

inferredMistakes.text: Confusing a free trade area with a customs union, assuming members must share a common external tariff policy (and so ruling out option A), when in fact that common external tariff is the distinguishing feature of a customs union, not a free trade area.
